summary:
EcoPulse Jogja is an innovative Web-GIS platform designed to tackle Yogyakarta’s decentralized waste crisis by connecting NASA orbital observations with community waste management. Ever since the closure of the Piyungan landfill, unmanaged organic waste has been piling up in temporary depots, releasing methane—a super-pollutant with a heat-trapping potency over 80 times greater than carbon dioxide.  
​To solve this, our platform captures NASA EMIT methane plume data to pinpoint high-emission hotspots across Sleman, Bantul, and Yogyakarta City. We then link these satellite insights with local waste depots to calculate the most efficient transport routes, diverting organic waste away from open-air decomposition straight into active bio-digesters.  
​This project is vital because it gives municipal leaders the real-time spatial intelligence needed to act fast, prevent environmental leaks, and transform everyday waste into clean biogas energy and organic fertilizer.
details: EcoPulse Jogja is an innovative Web-GIS platform that connects space-based Earth observations with community-level waste management logistics. Following the closure of the Piyungan landfill, unmanaged organic waste began piling up across temporary depots, emitting invisible methane—a super-pollutant with a heat-trapping potency over 80 times greater than carbon dioxide. Our system ingests NASA EMIT methane plume and enhancement datasets to pinpoint high-emission hotspots across Sleman, Bantul, and Yogyakarta City. By overlaying these orbital observations with local OpenStreetMap road networks and TPS3R (waste processing facility) coordinates, our spatial analytics engine automatically calculates the most efficient transport routes to divert rotting organic waste straight into active community bio-digesters.EcoPulse Jogja provides municipal authorities and village-level operators with real-time spatial intelligence. By stopping open-air organic decomposition, it mitigates over 80x climate potency per unit of diverted methane, eliminates foul odors and vector-borne disease risks near residential areas, and scales up circular waste-to-energy conversion by feeding clean organic feedstock into community bio-digesters to produce cooking gas and organic fertilizer.Data Sources: NASA EMIT L2B Methane Plume & Enhancement Data (60m cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs), U.S. Greenhouse Gas Center baselines, and local OpenStreetMap networks.
